page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 56 dedicated vCPUs and 56 physical cores running on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The instance is equipped with 224.0 GB of memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It includes no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 decompression single-threaded benchmarks scoring in the bottom 25%, while single-threaded gzip compression falls into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 decompression multi-threaded, consistently rank in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory and database operations, also demonstrate average performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads that can leverage its 56 dedicated physical cores to compensate for lower single-core speeds. The lack of bundled local storage and GPU hardware reduces baseline infrastructure costs, making it suitable for multi-threaded processing tasks. Recommended workloads include static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded data decompression, where parallel execution mitigates the weaker single-core performance.
